Yes — if you have a release dated at least two weeks out. Pre-saves turn fans into day-one saves, and saves in the first 48 hours are the strongest signal Spotify's algorithm reads for Release Radar and algorithmic push. The cost is near zero, but be realistic about scale: with 12,500 followers, expect modest numbers — the return depends on where you push the link. Your most engaged segment (42 tip-link clicks, 8 actual tips) is the core most likely to pre-save, so aim it there.

Which release is it for, and when does it drop?

examples.referenceWhy: It misses that Night Swim drops tomorrow (2026-10-30) and asks which release and date when it already has both. Its 'two weeks out' rule would also push the artist away from a pre-save that should go up today.

Start with one finished song. Not a catalog, not a strategy — one track you'd defend in public.

The order that works: finish that single, get it on a distributor (DistroKid, TuneCore, CD Baby — pick one, they all get you onto Spotify), then use the 2–4 weeks before release day to set up your profile and a promo runway here. Your profile is a blank slate right now — no bio, no links, no releases — which is fine, but it means everything you build lands on empty ground unless we fill it before launch.

Do you have a track already finished and mixed, or are you still writing? If one is done, tell me the title and I'll set up the release here so we can build a launch plan around it.
